text:
Incident Bot: Pager S2 - elevated inference tail latency observed in az1a (us-east-1a). Alert: resolver jitter + high DNS latency affecting inference pods. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dns-resolver-drift
zoe_oncall: ack, pulling up dashboards and traces. assigning until we know scope.
dave: graph shows 95th token latency spike ~30% above SLO starting ~3189991200. Resolver RT is spiking 200-800ms in az1a, other AZs steady.
maria: KV-cache miss rate increased, prefix/KV cache regen events correlated with DNS timeouts. some model instances returning 502s from runtime.
eng_runtime: seeing increased socket connect delays from inference frontends to model workers. Net logs show repeated NXDOMAIN or resolver timeouts then TCP reconnects.
sean: could be resolver drift / local dnsmasq loop. Can we steer traffic to eu-west while we mitigate? minimal risk.
zoe_oncall: steered ~20% of traffic from az1a -> eu-west1 via routing policy (temporary). command run: `redwoodctl route set --from az1a --to eu-west1 --percent 20 --reason "resolver jitter"`
support_bot: creating customer impact ticket TKT-5821; initial count ~15 customers showing degraded responses, 3 with >1% error rate. notifying SRE-svcs channel.
julia_ops: starting targeted pod drains on 2 affected node subgroups to force fresh DNS resolver binds. will cordon/drain + reattach ENIs if needed.
dave: running quick dig against node resolver, sample output:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +time=5 +tries=2 www.example.com @169.254.169.253
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 0
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;www.example.com. IN A
;; Query time: 482 msec
;; SERVER: 169.254.169.253#53(169.254.169.253)
;; WHEN: Tue Mar 15 12:20:34 UTC 2026
;; MSG SIZE  rcvd: 41
```
dave: lots of 300-600ms query times and occasional 5s timeouts.
eng_runtime: initiating model-fallback canary: roll out quantized-v2 as fallback for high-latency routes to keep latency low. config snippet: `rollout: {policy: canary, percent: 10, fallback_chain: [quantized-v2, quantized-v1]}`
zoe_oncall: also increasing DNS cache TTL at edge for inference frontends to reduce query volume: `redwoodctl config set inference.dns.cache_ttl 6m --env prod --reason "mitigate resolver jitter"`
sean: ops note: AWS ENI attach/teardown metrics for az1a show spike in detach/attach around same timeframe — could be control-plane flapping causing resolver bindings to be transient. Will request AWS support if we see ENI failures persist.
julia_ops: performing `kubectl drain` on node ip-10-0-23-45 (subset) to recycle dnsmasq. Commands:
```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-23-45
kubectl drain ip-10-0-23-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --network-interface-ids eni-0abcd1234efgh5678
```
julia_ops: brought up fresh nodes in az1b to absorb load if az1a continues to degrade. provisioning is ~4m ETA.
support_bot: customers with support severity >2 have been contacted with template: "We're investigating elevated inference latency in us-east-1a; routing controls applied; temporary mitigations in place; we'll follow up with a timeline."
maria: after TTL increase and initial drains, kv-cache regen rate decreased ~30%. still seeing some tail errors while canary fallback ramps.
dave: rolling window: errors peaked at +12 min and started trending down after routing and TTL change. still monitoring for DNS timeouts at node level.
eng_runtime: canary fallback scaled to 25% of requests for az1a traffic. latency p95 reduced back toward SLO for covered requests. will keep fallback until rollback safe.
zoe_oncall: handing off incident to ops lead julia_ops for long-running mitigation and customer comms. I'm leaving a summary: "resolver jitter caused by resolver host instability in az1a; mitigations: partial cross-region steer, DNS TTL increase, targeted node recycle, model fallback; initial customer impact ~15 customers degraded, no data loss, SLO risk mitigated by fallback. next: postmortem + AWS SR for ENI/control-plane behavior." :thumbsup:
julia_ops: ack. I will run the AWS SR and keep this channel updated. adding `#postmortem` owner: dave + maria + eng_runtime.
Incident Bot: Action log: steered 20% -> eu-west1 at 3189991250, increased dns cache ttl at 3189991260, started canary fallback at 3189991270, node drains begun at 3189991280.
support_bot: final note for now: open customer notifications created (TKT-5821, TKT-5822). will update with timeline in postmortem.
zoe_oncall: Good job team. Monitoring shows stabilizing metrics. If we see new spikes re-escalate.
julia_ops: will run hourly checks and post updates. planning postmortem doc and customer impact summary for SEs.
eng_runtime: logging rollback criteria: sustained p95 under SLO for 30m without routing steer.
Incident Bot: thread closed for active handoff at 3189991299 (status: oncall->ops handoff). Follow-ups: postmortem assigned, AWS SR open, customer comms ongoing.
